title: Morphisms from the spectrum of a field correspond to a point and a residue field embedding
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $x\in X$, with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ be the canonical morphism ($\operatorname{Spec}$ of the residue map $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\kappa(x)$ followed by the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$) [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $j_x$ maps the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ to $x$. Let $K$ be a field and $f:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ a morphism; put $x=f(\xi)$, $\xi$ the point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$, and let $\varphi_f:\kappa(x)\to K$ be the field map induced by the local homomorphism $f^\sharp_\xi:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K,\xi}=K$ (the map induced by $f$ on residue fields). Then $f=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_f)$, and $f\mapsto(f(\xi),\varphi_f)$ is a bijection from morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ to pairs $(x,\varphi)$ of a point $x\in X$ and a ring map $\varphi:\kappa(x)\to K$, with inverse $(x,\varphi)\mapsto j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$.
